evidence.limitation: Absolute latency and resource observations passed, but the issue-234 Java/Go comparison did not satisfy every variation and candidate-order condition. These thresholds are QA pilot operating limits, not production SLOs.

PolicySearchServiceErrorRate.suppression: Fewer than 20 requests or only success/invalid_request outcomes.
PolicySearchServiceErrorRate.recovery: The five-minute unexpected-error ratio returns to 10% or lower.
PolicySearchServiceErrorRate.response: Split failures by transport and status, inspect safe logs/traces, and verify Elasticsearch before rollback.

PolicySearchHighLatency.recovery: The five-minute request p95 returns to 250ms or lower.
PolicySearchHighLatency.response: Split latency by transport and inspect Elasticsearch duration and a representative trace.

PolicySearchElasticsearchFailure.recovery: The five-minute dependency failure ratio returns to 5% or lower.
PolicySearchElasticsearchFailure.response: Separate search from replace failures and verify Elasticsearch readiness, TLS and index privileges.

PolicySearchElasticsearchHighLatency.recovery: The five-minute dependency p95 returns to 250ms or lower.
PolicySearchElasticsearchHighLatency.response: Split search and replace latency, inspect Elasticsearch health and correlate a slow trace.

PolicySearchEventFailure.suppression: Fewer than 10 completed events, healthy idle or disabled workers.
PolicySearchEventFailure.recovery: The five-minute error/malformed/cancelled ratio returns to 10% or lower.
PolicySearchEventFailure.response: Split registered and terminated outcomes, inspect safe worker logs and verify writer readiness.

PolicySearchEventStalled.suppression: Worker enabled is zero or in-flight age is zero.
PolicySearchEventStalled.recovery: Completion or cancellation resets in-flight age to zero.
PolicySearchEventStalled.response: Identify the fixed event type, inspect writer/Kafka readiness and a correlated trace, then restart or roll back only after preserving offsets.

PolicySearchResourcePressure.suppression: Both CPU and memory remain at or below 80% of their deployment limits.
PolicySearchResourcePressure.recovery: Both resource signals remain below their thresholds.
PolicySearchResourcePressure.response: Inspect query/event load, runtime memory, throttling, pod events and rollout identity.

PolicySearchUnavailable.recovery: The deployment returns to its desired available replica count.
PolicySearchUnavailable.response: Inspect rollout, readiness, configuration, Elasticsearch and Kafka assignment before rollback.

PolicySearchTelemetryMissing.suppression: The deployment is unavailable or runtime samples are present.
PolicySearchTelemetryMissing.recovery: A bounded Go runtime sample resumes.
PolicySearchTelemetryMissing.response: Verify OTLP configuration, Alloy receiver and remote-write health before changing the rule.

PolicySearchTelemetryDeliveryFailure.suppression: Delivery failure/drop counters do not increase; missing exporter series do not fabricate failure.
PolicySearchTelemetryDeliveryFailure.recovery: All five-minute failure/drop increases return to zero.
PolicySearchTelemetryDeliveryFailure.response: Identify the failed signal/backend and inspect bounded retry/drop counters while preserving service availability.

PolicySearchTelemetryBacklog.suppression: No samples are pending and exporter queue use is 80% or lower; absent series do not fabricate backlog.
PolicySearchTelemetryBacklog.recovery: Pending samples clear and exporter queues return to 80% or lower.
PolicySearchTelemetryBacklog.response: Check backend reachability and Alloy queue/WAL health, then verify recovery within two minutes.

PolicySearchUnexpectedRestart.suppression: No container restart occurred in 15 minutes.
PolicySearchUnexpectedRestart.recovery: The last restart ages out of the 15-minute window.
PolicySearchUnexpectedRestart.response: Inspect prior state, safe logs, pod events, resource pressure and rollout identity.
